full_text: Australia usually hosts the world's biggest cuttlefish mating event - not this year According to official figures only 1,811 cuttlefish turned up to mate this year, down 97% on last year. Every winter, a sliver of the South Australian coast hosts the world's largest mating event for giant cuttlefish. Some years, hundreds of thousands of the unique marine species endemic to Australia gather along the Cuttlefish Coast for the annual mating season, bringing their colourful, shape-shifting figures to the shallow waters and attracting thousands of keen divers. But this year, the turnout was the lowest on record, sparking concerns of a "catastrophic decline" of the species. Official figures released this month estimate just 1,811 cuttlefish turned up to mate this year, down from 63,000 last year - a 97% drop. The state government says atoxic algal bloomthat has ravaged the state's coastline for more than 18 months may be to blame for the sharp decline. The low figures have also prompted calls for the species to be listed as endangered. Adult cuttlefish typically die after breeding so each mating season is crucial for the species' future, but in recent months, just 440 eggs have been counted, instead of the millions that are usually laid. Manny Katz, 28, was one of four divers who spent hours along the coast last month to observe the annual breeding event, having been tasked by South Australia's Department of Environment and Water (DEW). "Because there have been so few cuttlefish, DEW thought it would be worth going out and trying to do an assessment of how many eggs there currently are around the coastline to understand what the population is going to be next year."

The journey is made possible by the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan highway, which winds through the rugged mountains of Central Asia, a project under the Belt and Road Initiative proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping. Shipment will be expedited as the three countries are also seeing the construction of another major cross-border project -- the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway -- aimed at improving the well-being of people along the route. The expanding connectivity across Central Asia offers a glimpse into a broader vision Xi has championed over the years: to pursue friendships and partnerships with China's neighbors and foster an amicable, secure and prosperous neighborhood. Xi arrived in Bishkek on Sunday for a state visit to Kyrgyzstan, China's neighbor to the west, and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit , a major move of his neighborhood diplomacy. "WISH OUR NEIGHBORS WELL" Xi's upcoming trip to Kyrgyzstan will be his third visit to the country as Chinese president, following previous visits in 2013 and 2019. Titled “No Tricks! Blink, You’re Gone!”, the mural was designed by Iranian artist Danial Farrokh and alludes to reports that Trump was secretly moved from Air Force One in Turkey via a catering truck and transferred to another aircraft amid fears of an Iranian attack, Mehr reported on Saturday. The large-scale artwork depicts a magician performing a trick while pointing toward a catering truck containing an image of Trump. Several white doves fly across the scene, adding to the imagery of a stage performance and illusion. Located in one of Tehran’s major thoroughfares, the mural joins a series of large-scale works displayed in the capital that use public art to comment on current political developments and international affairs. The new artwork was created under the auspices of Art Bureau, an institution that has frequently used murals and other visual works in public spaces to address social, political and cultural themes. full_text: One killed, five wounded in shooting at rave party in Switzerland One person was killed and five others wounded, some seriously, after gunfire broke out at a rave party in Aarau, northern Switzerland, police said One person was killed and five others wounded, some seriously, after gunfire broke out at a rave party in Aarau, northern Switzerland, police said A shooting at an annual techno rave in Aarau, north of Zurich, left one person dead and five others injured early Sunday, prompting a large-scale manhunt to locate the unidentified attackers. "The search for the perpetrators, whose identities are currently unknown, is under way," police said on X, adding that the motive and exact circumstances of the shooting remained unclear. Police launched what they described as a "large-scale response" following the incident. AnAFPjournalist saw armed officers deployed along the highway as far as 30 kilometres (18 miles) from the scene. Swiss newspaper Blick reported that the shooting took place before 3:00 am (0100 GMT) near the Aarauer Rave. Around 3,500 people attended the annual techno event, which ran from 3:00 pm on Saturday until 2:00 am on Sunday. Police spokeswoman Vanessa Rumpold was quoted by Blick as saying the shooting took place at the racecourse where the event was held. "Several shots were fired within a large group of people," she said. Witnesses told Blick that gunfire erupted at about 2:30 am, while the rave was still under way. Many people sought shelter in a nearby gymnasium, with some partygoers initially believing the sounds were fireworks. One witness described hearing a "burst of gunfire". full_text: Pacific leaders meet in Palau as drug crime rises, China-Taiwan tensions simmer Pacific Islands Forum leaders will focus on transnational drug crime, climate change and other regional priorities in Palau, while tensions involving China, Taiwan and the US threaten to dominate the summit Pacific Islands Forum leaders will focus on transnational drug crime, climate change and other regional priorities in Palau, while tensions involving China, Taiwan and the US threaten to dominate the summit Pacific island leaders will meet in Palau from Monday for the Pacific Islands Forum summit, where they are expected to strengthen regional cooperation against transnational drug crime while addressing climate change, food security and renewable energy. Palau, host of the 18-member forum this year, is one of three Pacific countries that maintains diplomatic relations with Taiwan rather than China. Beijing is also a major creditor to many Pacific island states. China, Taiwan and the United States are among the forum's invited aid partners, although they will not take part in the leaders' meeting. Beijing has objected to Taiwan's invitation. Taiwan's Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung joined Palau President Surangel Whipps on Sunday to open a fleet of electric buses donated by Taipei. China responded to Lin's arrival by declaring Palau, which relies heavily on tourism, an "unsafe" destination for travellers, Whipps later told reporters. Chinese tourists make up the largest group of visitors to Palau, according to data. The US Embassy accused Beijing of trying to "weaponize tourism to coerce Palau". full_text: ‘No safe seat for Labor’: Far-right One Nation scores historic WA win, puts Albanese’s party on notice Australia’s One Nation party has claimed its first Lower House seat in the Western Australian state Parliament, with its candidate Luke Herdegen securing 57 per cent of the votes with around 75 per cent of the ballots counted Australia’s One Nation party has claimed its first Lower House seat in the Western Australian state Parliament, with its candidate Luke Herdegen securing 57 per cent of the votes with around 75 per cent of the ballots counted Australia’s One Nation party has claimed its first Lower House seat in the Western Australian state Parliament, with its candidate Luke Herdegen securing 57 per cent of the votes with around 75 per cent of the ballots counted. He defeated his Labor rival, who received 43 per cent of the vote. The seat was previously held by Labor leader Paul Papalia, who won it in 2025 with approximately 47 per cent of the vote. The Liberal candidate in that election secured just over 8 per cent. However, Papalia announced his retirement in July, citing a family medical issue, triggering the by-election. Since the Labor Party holds an absolute majority in the state Parliament, One Nation’s victory is not expected to directly affect the stability of the government. However, the sharp increase in support for the far-right party is likely to deliver a political and moral blow to Labor. After his victory, Herdegen said there were no longer any safe Labor seats in Western Australia or the country. “There are no safe Labor seats in this state or in this country any more.
